correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge3\), the unique-earlier-neighbor rule characterizes every order-generated graph matching. A complete order-case partition yields exactly two groups of \(n+1\) high facets and \(3n\) mixed edges; explicit orders realize every one. Each high group deformation retracts onto its central simplex. Collapsing both contractible subcomplexes gives the two-vertex \(3n\)-edge graph, hence \( igvee^{3n-1}S^1\). The relative homology exact sequence gives the integral sum-zero lattice and its \(S_n\) action, while direct face counting gives the formula. A separate executable enumerates every vertex order at \(2\le n\le7\), compares all faces and checks mod-two Betti numbers. Finite tests corroborate, but the infinite statement is proved symbolically.

value.rationale: The first genuinely bipartite two-center family beyond path/star/cycle examples has strong Morse complexes with unbounded maximal simplex dimension but uniformly graph-like homotopy; the complete facet and integral \(S_n\)-homology descriptions explain the unexpected collapse mechanism. This is a natural comparison to known ordinary Morse \(K_{2,n}\) complexes, which instead support high-dimensional homology. The result supplies reusable bridge/relative-homology structure, not a one-off finite census or parameter re-labeling.
